decision.title: Streamed xsl:merge (MERGE) and capture="yes" end rules while streaming (packet 7.6g)

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . Makes 's two designs; replaces 's "merge sources are grounded" and "capture="yes" end rules while streaming" not done. Verified as asks: the debug preset, the stream, xslt, IR and evaluator part unit tests, clang-tidy on the files changed, tools/check-call-cycles.py, and the whole XT40 suite with the release driver, compared case by case.

item.p: MERGE (src/ir_internal.h; glossary , ): an xsl:merge one to 16 of whose sources stream becomes a new IR kind, evaluated by the stream part (src/evaluator_stream.c). A source streams when it is streamable, has for-each-source (no for-each-item), does not sort before merging, validates nothing, names no accumulators, and its select is a path of child steps without predicates from the document node whose last step selects elements (striding, 19.8.8; a crawling or sorted source is XTSE3430 already); nothing in it or the merge action reads fn:last, fn:path or fn:has-children (the number of groups is not known while streaming). Other sources are grounded first, their tuples sorted and checked as before, and are one more cursor. A merge stream (new unit table, sxml_ir_unit_add_merge_streams) is the anchors' URIs and an OPENS_DOCUMENT STREAM over a chain of child-step STREAMs whose last body is the source's tuple: the IR of a stream point, read by MERGE as the description of its cursors, which pull one selected node at a time from the stream builder (), skip what no step can select, and ground the selected element in a full window; a document the resolver gives as a tree is walked. Rejected: a cursor as a suspended STREAM task (one task stack: k cursors cannot each keep a suspended chain), and a comparison function of its own (the grounded merge's sort and grouping decide the order and equality, so collations, data types and orders are those of 15.4 by construction).

Stepping (15.4, 15.6): each step binds heads to the open group's first tuple and every cursor's current tuple and evaluates order, the first run of equal keys of the sorted heads (a stable sort, so the group's first tuple stays first among equal keys). Without an open group the run opens one; with one, a run that holds its first tuple and others extends it, one that holds it alone closes it, and one without it is XTDE2220 (a cursor's next tuple sorts before the one it had). The cursors taken move on. A closed group's tuples are put in source, anchor and input order and the action runs on the group array [tuples, key] as before (current-merge-group, -key, -key-array, the named groups), its position the group's number, delivered when the merge delivers (). Errors so come in input order: merge-077's XTDE3490 is raised before a later XTDE2220.

capture="yes" (19.9): sxml_ir_stream_accumulators.capture, the new function stream-capture-0($node), gives the numbers of the accumulators declared streamable one of whose capturing end rules matches an element; it is called at each element's start (a call like the initial one, before the start calls), and the stream builder then also sends the element's events to a full window of its own (glossary ; nested tees a stack, an empty element's tee ended at once), whose element those accumulators' end calls get as the node (others keep the shallow window, so their reads of accumulator values still find the node). A stylesheet whose streamable accumulators capture now streams (sxml_xslt_accumulators_stream removed).

Measured (release): sxml transform merging two generated 38.3 MB documents of 600,000 records each by id, peak resident 1,055.6 MB before (grounded), 11.0 MB after, output identical (24.6 s and 30.0 s, the second beside a suite run); evaluator_stream_test merges two 1.2 MB documents with an allocator peak of 502 KB under a 1 MB limit the grounded merge exceeds. XT40 (whole suite, case by case): 11,943 to 11,945 passed, none lost (merge-077, merge-079). Cases that stream now: merge 21 (039, 040, 041, 062, 063, 070 to 072, 074, 076 to 081, 083, 090, 091, 098, 100, 101), si-merge 6 of 6; capture 5 compute their capturing accumulators while streaming (201, 202, 204, 206, 207), 3 of them through tees.

Left (lowered grounded, same results by 19.10): merge sources with validation or type (merge-049 to -053), use-accumulators (merge-051, -065 to -067, -082), predicates, or more than 16 streamed sources; merge actions reading fn:last; capture-206 fails as before (an unstreamed difference); merge-097's collection URI ().
